new_alerts.thesis: NeOnc Technologies stands out for the depth and persistence of its insider signal: Chairman/CEO Amir Heshmatpour and CEO Thomas C. Chen have made repeated open-market cash purchases from November 2025 through mid-August 2026 (roughly $1 million cumulative), including buys made in the days immediately after the company's binary Phase 2a data event -- a strong statement of management conviction rather than opportunistic buying on a dip alone. That data event delivered a genuine positive catalyst: NEO100 met its primary endpoint in recurrent IDH1-mutant high-grade glioma on August 12, 2026, with statistically significant progression-free survival benefit and a clean safety profile, opening a path toward an FDA Type B registrational meeting. Institutional support has been building into the event, with $14.08 million of inflows over the trailing year, 13 institutional buyers versus 2 sellers, and three sell-side initiations (Maxim Group, Alliance Global Partners, BTIG). This is flagged as an early-stage watch rather than a high-conviction one because the technical setup does not resemble a clean multi-month base-and-breakout: the stock fell roughly 55% over the trailing six months before this month's 34% recovery, and the August 12 data day itself produced a large single-day price swing rather than gradual accumulation, so the technical/setup dimension of the rubric is weak even though the insider, institutional, and catalyst dimensions are unusually strong for a name this size.
new_alerts.risks: Binary clinical-catalyst risk is inherent to a clinical-stage biopharma name -- the Phase 2a readout, while positive on its primary endpoint, was a single-day event that could reverse on follow-up data, subgroup results, or FDA feedback; the stock's 6-month decline of roughly 55% prior to this month's rebound and thin overall institutional ownership relative to peers mean liquidity and volatility risk are elevated, and the technical pattern does not match a textbook gradual, low-volatility base-and-breakout.

However, there is still no confirmed insider open-market buying in the review window (GuruFocus flags $384.3M of insider selling over the trailing 12 months), institutional ownership remains 'minimal' in absolute terms per MarketBeat, and analyst sentiment is unusually split (targets from $25 to $65, with Wall Street Zen still cautious even as Jefferies and KeyBanc are bullish), reflecting genuine uncertainty about near-term execution. Volume has dropped sharply from its post-IPO/post-selloff highs, consistent with a name still finding a stable base rather than confirming a breakout.
watchlist.risks: As a recent IPO with a short trading history, technical base is not yet well established; the stock diluted shareholders with a $48/share secondary offering in May 2026 and faces intensified SpaceX-driven competitive pressure that has already triggered one significant selloff.

watchlist.thesis: Oklo remains a well-covered, high-profile advanced-nuclear name with real DOE regulatory and fuel-supply momentum (Aurora Powerhouse safety design approval, Centrus HALEU letter of intent, plutonium program selection, and the Groves reactor's first criticality), but the stock is still working through a post-earnings pullback that bottomed near $37.80-$39.48 in late July before a partial bounce into the low-$40s. There is still no open-market insider buying — recent Form 4s remain RSU vesting, option exercises, and tax-withholding sales, plus a CEO Form 144 sale notice — and analysts continue trimming near-term targets (Truist to $51, Texas Capital to $89) even while staying structurally bullish (consensus ~$80 target, Texas Capital naming it a top pick). This still looks like a name working off an overextended prior rally rather than a fresh accumulation setup; nothing has materially changed since the prior write-up.
watchlist.risks: Company remains pre-revenue at scale (first quarterly revenue was just $1.21M in Q2 2026) with a wide EPS loss, so the investment case rests entirely on execution of a multi-year reactor buildout; heavy insider selling (RSU/option-driven plus a CEO Form 144 filing) and short-seller attention add near-term technical risk.
